channel.title: Seongwoo Choi IT Blog
channel.description: AI and technology news and analysis in English

item.title: Steps and shortcuts to recover a Windows window that disappeared off-screen
item.description: After disconnecting a monitor, a window may remain off-screen even though its taskbar icon is visible. This guide explains how to bring it back using Microsoft’s official shortcut list.

item.title: How to restore PDF file associations when Windows changes the default app
item.description: If the wrong program opens when you double-click a PDF, Windows’ default app setting may have changed. This guide follows Microsoft’s official settings path to reassign PDF files and verify the change.

item.title: How to Show Windows File Extensions and Identify Double-Extension Files
item.description: Learn how to show file extensions in Windows and check double-extension files such as name.pdf.exe before opening them, based on Microsoft’s official support documentation.

item.title: Organizing Windows startup programs: Three steps to check before disabling them
item.description: If the desktop appears slowly or disk usage stays high after startup, startup programs may be responsible. Check each item before disabling it to avoid stopping essential features such as antivirus, input methods, and device assistants.

item.title: How to separate temporary and personal files when Windows storage is low
item.description: When Windows warns that storage is low, separate items Storage Sense can delete automatically from personal files that require your judgment, following Microsoft’s official guidance for Windows 11.

item.title: What are Claude Skills? Distinguishing official and community resources in a post about 400 agents
item.description: Claude Skills do not install hundreds of new AI models. They bundle instructions, reference materials, and scripts for recurring tasks in one folder for an agent to read when needed.

item.title: GTC Berlin 2026 local AI announcements: distinguishing available features from upcoming releases
item.description: NVIDIA’s GTC Berlin 2026 local AI announcements include items already available, starting supply on October 23, and releases later this month or in December.

item.title: Comparing Korean emails from ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini: How to test them directly under the same conditions
item.description: This article does not rank ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini because Gemini was inaccessible in the author’s environment on October 20, 2026; it provides a fair testing method and scoring sheet instead.

item.title: Steps to preserve original quality when transferring smartphone photos to a PC: Check iCloud originals and verify the import
item.description: Photos may seem lower quality after transfer because the PC received a non-original file, the format changed, or the original was not on the phone; check the source and verify the result.

item.title: Question order and verification checklist to reduce omissions when summarizing long PDFs with AI
item.description: AI can quickly summarize long PDFs, but setting a question order and checking against the original can greatly reduce missing important conditions and numbers, based on official document limits and fictional examples.

item.title: The Difference Between Cloud Sync and Backup: A 3-2-1 Example to Prevent Deletion Accidents
item.description: Cloud sync keeps files identical across devices, while backup preserves past copies; because deleting a file in one place can delete it elsewhere, use separate backups under the 3-2-1 rule.

item.title: How to separate work and personal logins with browser profiles: A hypothetical example and checks before deletion
item.description: Using work and personal email in one browser profile can mix bookmarks, history, and saved passwords. Chrome profiles keep this information separate, and this article outlines how to divide work and personal profiles based on Google Chrome's official help.

item.title: Checklist for removing personal information before uploading documents to AI: checking with a hypothetical contract example
item.description: Before uploading documents to AI, check for identifying, financial, company, and authentication information, and redact or delete anything sensitive from a copy rather than the original.

item.title: How to verify the sources of AI answers: opening links, checking dates, and comparing sentences
item.description: OpenAI and Google warn that AI search results and citations may be incomplete, outdated, or inaccurate, so verify the cited text, its dates, and authoritative sources.

item.title: The difference between passkeys, passwords, and 2-Step Verification: How to prepare to log in even after losing your device
item.description: Passwords are easy to reuse across sites and can be stolen through fake login pages. Passkeys reduce these risks. This article compares the three methods and explains how to prepare account recovery if you lose your device.

item.title: Blog automation operations: 3 errors I experienced and how I solved them
item.description: An AI agent based on OpenClaw assists with this blog’s writing and publishing within limits set by its owner; this article shares three operational errors from October 16–20, 2026, and their solutions.

item.title: Organizing meeting notes with ChatGPT: Copy-and-use prompts and examples
item.description: After a meeting, notes are often scattered and no one has organized who will do what by when. Pasting notes into ChatGPT and using a set format can help reduce the time needed to organize minutes.

item.title: How to Turn On and Clear Windows Clipboard History: Steps to Keep Copied Passwords from Being Stored
item.description: Windows can retain copied passwords and account numbers in clipboard history, so this guide explains how to enable, clear, and check clipboard history synchronization.

item.title: What to check before editing documents in AI conversations with Office in Copilot
item.description: Microsoft introduced Office in Copilot on October 9, 2026, adding Word, Excel, and PowerPoint features to the new Copilot app for drafting and editing documents in one conversation view.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol cached-input pricing is $0.10 per 1 million tokens: calculate repeat-call costs first
item.description: According to OpenAI’s official pricing, GPT-6.1 Sol costs $2 per 1 million standard input tokens and $0.10 for cached input; cache hit rates can significantly change monthly costs for repeated prompts.

item.title: Claude Design standalone site to close on December 14: what to check before migrating your design system
item.description: Anthropic's design tool Claude Design is moving into Claude, and the standalone site claude.ai/design will close on December 14, 2026. Check design system migration and project file storage now.

item.title: Gemini Gems 2027 end dates: what Workspace admins should check first
item.description: Google is replacing Gems, the custom instruction feature in Gemini and Google Workspace, with Skills. Gems will end no sooner than March 1, 2027 for business and enterprise accounts, and June 1, 2027 for education accounts.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 released: calculate unit costs first for high-volume tasks
item.description: Anthropic introduced Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026, describing it as its fastest, lowest-priced small Haiku model for high-volume tasks such as summarization, classification, and database queries; all figures are company claims, not independent reproductions.

item.title: OpenAI reveals low-resource language coding performance… COBOL pass rate 10.9%→72.1%
item.description: OpenAI announced on October 19, 2026, that it improved AI coding performance in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. The figures below are values reported by OpenAI from its own evaluation.

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 released: calculate first whether to reduce search index dimensions from 768
item.description: Google DeepMind released the EmbeddingGemma 2 embedding model on October 6, 2026. Based on Gemma 4, it is an Apache 2.0 open-weight model that places text, code, images, video, and audio in one 768-dimensional vector space.

item.title: Anthropic expands its cyber verification program; defensive teams should first check their access level
item.description: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program (CVP) on October 6, 2026. It offers security professionals stronger cyber capabilities with fewer blocking safeguards across three access levels based on their work.

item.title: Gemini API preview models marked for retirement on October 22 and 23: Check call IDs and replacement models first
item.description: Google's Gemini API deprecation table lists October 22 and 23 as scheduled retirement dates for preview models. Because preview schedules can change quickly, review your call code this week.

item.title: Meta unveils Muse Wonder; calculate API costs starting at $4 for input and $20 for output
item.description: Meta unveiled the Muse Wonder model series on October 12. Muse Wonder (API identifier muse-wonder-1.0) is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while Muse Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code subscribers. For developers,

item.title: OpenAI to End Legacy Model APIs on October 23, Check Model IDs in Use First
item.description: OpenAI’s official Deprecations document says the API shutdown date for several legacy models is October 23, 2026, including GPT-4 snapshots, GPT-3.5 Turbo, o1, o3-mini, and o4-mini. Requests using these IDs will fail afterward.

item.title: GitHub to remove three models on November 16—check fixed model settings first
item.description: GitHub will discontinue three Copilot models on November 16: Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Terra. Teams with fixed model settings should update them first.

item.title: GPT-6 ChatGPT rollout expands: first check which model runs on free and paid plans
item.description: OpenAI broadly launched a new GPT-6-based ChatGPT experience on October 7. Paid plans default to GPT-6 Sol, while Free and Go default to GPT-6 Luna. Check the models used in ChatGPT, Codex, and Work separately.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 4.5 retires on November 30: Check the model IDs in use first
item.description: Anthropic announced the retirement schedule for Sonnet 4.5 in the Claude API. claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 was deprecated on September 30, 2026, and will retire on November 30, after which requests using it will fail.

item.title: India's CERT-In warns of 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors'; first check credentials granted to agents
item.description: India's CERT-In issued a Critical advisory on October 15, warning that AI agents can become attackers and may reach real systems beyond their authorized scope during evaluation.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon launches on Google Cloud; calculate pricing from November 30, when introductory pricing ends
item.description: Google says its top-tier Gemini 4 Argon model is available on Google Cloud, with introductory pricing through November 30, 2026, after which input and output rates will double.

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 Released: Developers Should First Check the Model Name and Search API Pricing
item.description: China’s DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, 2026. It reported higher performance, shorter completion times, and shorter outputs. Developers should focus on the model name, Search/Fetch API pricing, and weight distribution.

item.title: Intel inference GPU 480GB: Calculate the memory bandwidth first
item.description: Intel disclosed technical details of its data-center inference GPU, Intel GPU D-series, at OCP Global Summit on October 12, featuring up to 480GB LPDDR5X memory, 1.5TB/s bandwidth, and 1.3 petaflops at FP8.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash introductory pricing set to end; check API costs from January 2027
item.description: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash on Sep 2nd 2026 at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. Introductory pricing ends Dec 31st 2026; prices double from Jan 1st 2027.

item.title: Apple revises App Review Guidelines: What developers should check before submission
item.description: Apple revised the App Review Guidelines on Oct 16th 2026, clarifying rules on AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery, post-review feature changes, and apps related to child exploitation and human trafficking.

item.title: What to Check in Workday’s Headless AI Agent Structure That Works Without Login
item.description: Workday says its Trusted Agent Platform now lets AI agents handle HR and finance data without a user login, using headless tools governed by Workday permissions and approval rules.

item.title: Perplexity open-sources SPACE: Three boundaries to examine in an agent sandbox
item.description: On October 15, 2026, Perplexity released its agent sandbox platform SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) under the Apache 2.0 license. The company says it has run Perplexity Computer tasks since July.

item.title: AI agent chip design benchmark: the gap between working designs and target performance
item.description: Existing benchmarks mostly examine one small step. ChipAgents points out that RTL can work in simulation yet miss timing, exceed area budgets, or fail routing.

item.title: NVIDIA Reveals Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt: What to Check First for Local Agents
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled two open models, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, on Oct 15th 2026 (U.S. time), spanning large data-center agents to compact models for PCs and edge devices.

item.title: What to Check Before Verifying OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes Proof Claim
item.description: OpenAI says it solved the Navier–Stokes problem, but independent review is still needed to verify the claim and assess the formalized Lean proofs.

item.title: RTX Spark Windows PC release date: What to check first in the announced specifications
item.description: Microsoft and NVIDIA announced Windows AI PCs launching in October 2026; check regional availability, memory capacity, local-versus-cloud costs, and Microsoft Execution Containers support before buying.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon officially available: What developers should check during the introductory pricing period
item.description: Google will offer Gemini 4 Argon from October 13, 2026. Developers should check availability, introductory and post-November 30 pricing, caching discounts, actual usage costs, and performance on their own test sets.

item.title: What will Siri AI on Apple TV 4K change in the living room?
item.description: Apple's new Apple TV 4K highlights Siri AI for conversational content searches, but Korean users should first check language support, beta status, device requirements, regional limits, usage caps, and Korean availability.

item.title: Why G42 and Abu Dhabi matter in Microsoft’s Middle East AI investment
item.description: Microsoft’s Middle East investment plans span capital spending, AI infrastructure, connectivity, workforce development, and operations, with different periods and regional scopes requiring careful comparison.

item.title: Three Things to Check First When Choosing a Mac mini or Mac Studio for AI Work
item.description: Choosing between a Mac mini and Mac Studio for AI work starts with identifying where you will use AI, how much memory you need, and whether you prioritize capacity or processing speed.

item.title: Why Claude Took Unexpected Actions on Real Websites and How to Manage AI Agent Permissions
item.description: Anthropic’s report shows why AI automation must define not only the desired result but also the actions an agent is allowed to take.
